The heart: the bulge, the icon, and 3 options

#929, your words: in its little icon picture … it doesn’t look the same as when you actually add it … the line bulges out near the bottom of the heart.

What is wrong now

1 · The bulge near the bottom

Left: the real heart’s lower-left side, drawn as an outline, the knee circled. Right: Edit Points on it (PC).

Each lower side has one point (the second dot up from the tip) whose handle is tiny and aimed 10° off the straight run coming up from the tip. So the side goes dead straight, then turns all at once at that point: a knee. It bends about 12× more sharply there than anywhere on the lobes (measured: 45 against 3.7).

2 · The icon is a different drawing

The Add-menu icon’s outline (white) laid over the heart you actually get (pink), same size; right, its lower-left side close up.

The tile is not drawn from the heart. It is a hand-typed picture in js/addmenu.js, copied from a draft of the v4.85 heart whose lower handles pointed straight up. So the icon dips in and juts out at that same spot (the funny little lines), and it never followed the heart when the heart changed.

The icon fix, so no shape can drift again

Draw the tile from the shape itself, with the same code that already draws the Squircle tile and every shape on pages 2–4. Then the tile is whatever the heart is, forever. Triangle, Plus, Arrow, Chevron, Trapezoid and Parallelogram are hand-typed copies too, so they get the same treatment, plus a test that fails if any tile with a shape behind it is hand-drawn again.

Now: your phone’s first Shape page, actual size.

After: every tile drawn from its shape, with heart A.

Every other tile in that first block is an outline, so an outline heart keeps the row even; the shape inside it is now exactly the heart you get. Say tile filled if you would rather it be solid.

The heart itself: 3 options

Now (what ships)

The v4.85 heart, drawn from your reference in v4.21.

Lower-left side as an outline · Edit Points (PC). Sharpest bend on the lower side: 45 — the knee (the round lobes are about 3.7; lower is smoother)

The bend near the bottom, and the icon above it that does not match.

A · Yours, fixed(recommended)

The same heart, with 2 of its 8 points changed.

Lower-left side as an outline · Edit Points (PC). Sharpest bend on the lower side: 2.1 (the round lobes are about 3.7; lower is smoother)

Same size, notch, lobes and point as the heart you approved. Only the two lower points change: their handle now lies along the straight side and is about 2½× longer, so the side curves into the lobe gradually. Edit Points shows the same 8 points.

B · Google’s heart

Material Symbols favorite — Apache 2.0. Fitted to Google’s outline to within 0.3% of the heart’s size.

Lower-left side as an outline · Edit Points (PC). Sharpest bend on the lower side: 3.8 (the round lobes are about 3.7; lower is smoother)

The heart on most apps’ like buttons: rounder lobes, a shallower notch, a little wider than tall (1.09 : 1), so it arrives a bit wider than today.

C · The textbook heart

A square turned on its corner with a half-circle on each top side — plain geometry, no licence. Fitted to within 0.3%.

Lower-left side as an outline · Edit Points (PC). Sharpest bend on the lower side: 3.5 (the round lobes are about 3.7; lower is smoother)

Perfectly round lobes and straight sides. Where each lobe meets its straight side there is still a faint shoulder: that is the construction, not a fault.

Reply heart A, heart B or heart C (and tile filled if you want the tile solid). The icon fix goes in with whichever you pick.
